test_name: Cross-validation is agent-grouped and time-ordered, never a random row split
description: Fold count equals folds x repeats; no agent appears in both a fold's training and test rows; every training row's T7 window closes before the earliest test-row submission in that fold (no training on the future); the inner validation split used for calibration is itself grouped and time-ordered; every test-period agent is tested exactly once per repeat; repeats redraw the agent grouping; folds are reproducible from a fixed seed.
test_data: The seed-42 dataset under config/model.yaml's 5-fold x 3-repeat scheme.
expected_result: Every grouping, ordering and reproducibility property holds for all folds and repeats. (This is the project's documented deviation from the literal DR-03 text, which specifies a random stratified 70:15:15 split; CLAUDE.md forbids random row splits for this domain, so the implemented design is agent-grouped, time-ordered repeated CV instead, and DR-03 is correctly marked 'not met' as written.)

test_name: Distribution primitives match their configured shape

test_name: Cost matrix, calibration and decision-band mechanics compute correctly

test_name: Agent, customer and device populations have the declared structure, and no agent-identifying attribute reaches the public frame

test_name: The anchor contract compiles reproducibly and exposes only the anchoring interface

test_name: A batch is anchored as an RFC 6962 root, and anchoring itself is audited
description: Working the anchoring queue cuts a contiguous batch of events since the last anchor, computes its Merkle root, submits it, and stores the returned transaction hash and block against that batch; the anchoring event is itself written to the audit log, inside the chain the next batch covers; batches are cut no more than once per ANCHOR_INTERVAL_SECONDS, except while clearing a backlog; a batch never exceeds ANCHOR_MAX_LEAVES; nothing is cut when no blockchain is configured.

expected_result: Every batching, timing and recording property holds.
actual_result: Pass (382/383 non-live pass, 2026-11-09 full run; 38 live-service tests pass when run against live services -- see app/BUILD_LOG.md).

test_name: An unreachable chain never blocks the app, and backlog clears on recovery
description: A submission and an approval both succeed, making no chain call at all, while the configured chain is down; events accumulate, chained but unanchored, and are anchored in full once the chain is reachable again; failed attempts retry with doubling delay and escalate to every administrator after the configured limit; an administrator can resume a stalled batch.
test_data: A fake chain client switched between up/down/revert/timeout modes.
expected_result: No user action blocks; the backlog is cleared on the next successful run; escalation and manual resume both work.
actual_result: Pass (382/383 non-live pass, 2026-11-09 full run; 38 live-service tests pass when run against live services -- see app/BUILD_LOG.md).

test_name: Resending an anchor, or racing two senders, is always harmless

test_data: A fake chain exercising each race condition.
expected_result: No batch is ever anchored, or recorded as failed, incorrectly.
actual_result: Pass (382/383 non-live pass, 2026-11-09 full run; 38 live-service tests pass when run against live services -- see app/BUILD_LOG.md).

test_name: A tampered audit log is never given a fresh anchor

test_name: The database refuses a batch that skips, overlaps, overruns the chain or miscounts, and keeps a confirmed anchor final
